messages.author: a29d08eaf6145f43
messages.subject: commonfactorGWAS parallel processing problem
parts:
Hi all,

New researcher here exploring the utility of GSEM in ALS research. I've sent it for a test drive using 4 traits (will be using many more in the future) but have gotten stumped when trying to run common factor GWAS.

Turns out, when specifying 'parallel=TRUE', the processes just seem to go to endless sleep with our computer architecture, even if tested on only 1-100 SNPs. However, if 'parallel=FALSE', the processes run on every thread available (n = 88) hindering the rest of our lab's work. We're aware that specifying the number of cores is pointless with 'parallel=FALSE' (tried it anyway, same result). Additionally, even with these 4 traits running on 88 threads, every SNP still takes 3 secs to be processed.

This seems like a bug or incompatibility of sorts so we're wondering if anyone has encountered a similar problem and can provide us with some wisdom and possible solutions - thank you!

Example code:
NEURO_factor_50SNP <- commonfactorGWAS(covstruc = LDSCoutput, SNPs = NEURO_sumstats_50SNP, estimation = "DWLS", cores = 1, toler = FALSE, SNPSE = FALSE, parallel = FALSE,GC="standard",MPI=FALSE)

Cheers,
Tomas

Apologies, turns out the solution was in section 1.1 of the tutorial. Problem solved!

Kind regards,
Tomas

messages.author: 0bde75ae837ce039
messages.subject: Re: commonfactorGWAS parallel processing problem
parts:
Hi GenomicSEM teams/users,
I'm using GenomicSEM, but it gets stuck for a long time when the common factor steps come. I'm running in an HPC cluster. Below is my job script and R script. Could you please guide me on how I can run this fast?

I appreciate your time and help.

Kind regards

Tania 

Job script:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#!/bin/bash -l
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=10
#SBATCH --mem=50G
#SBATCH --job-name=genomicsem
#SBATCH --time=6:00:00
#SBATCH --partition=general
#SBATCH --account=a_moni
#SBATCH -o genomicsem.output
#SBATCH -e genomicsem.error

cd $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR

# Set environment variables to limit threads
export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export MKL_NUM_THREADS=1
export NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1
export VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1

module load r

# Set up the environment for R
export PATH=/scratch/project_mnt/S0187/GenomicSEM/R-4.4.0/bin:$PATH


# Run the R script
Rscript genomicsem.R

#------------------my R script--------------------------------------------------------------
# Load necessary libraries
library(GenomicSEM)


# Munge step
hi <- "HillWD_MTAG_household_Income_formated.txt"
sd <- "TDI_GCST90013973_build37_formatted.txt"
oi <- "GWAS_hourly_wage_UKB_OI_formated.txt"
files <- c(hi, sd, oi)
hm3 <- "eur_w_ld_chr/w_hm3.snplist"
trait.names <- c("HI", "SD", "OI")
N = c(505541, 407271, 282963)
info.filter = 0.9
maf.filter = 0.01

munge(files = files, hm3 = hm3, trait.names = trait.names, N = N, info.filter = info.filter, maf.filter = maf.filter)

# Run LDSC
traits <- c("HI.sumstats.gz", "SD.sumstats.gz", "OI.sumstats.gz")
sample.prev <- c(NA, NA, NA)
population.prev <- c(NA, NA, NA)
ld <- "eur_w_ld_chr/"
wld <- "eur_w_ld_chr/"
hi_sd_oi_LDSCoutput <- ldsc(traits, sample.prev, population.prev, ld, wld, trait.names)
hi_sd_oi_LDSCoutput$V
hi_sd_oi_LDSCoutput$S
hi_sd_oi_LDSCoutput$m
k <- nrow(hi_sd_oi_LDSCoutput$S)
SE <- matrix(0, k, k)
SE[lower.tri(SE, diag = TRUE)] <- sqrt(diag(hi_sd_oi_LDSCoutput$V))

# Prepare the sumstats for GWAS
files <- c(hi, sd, oi)
ref <- "reference.1000G.maf.0.005.txt"
trait.names <- c("HI", "SD", "OI")
se.logit <- c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)
OLS <- c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE)
info.filter <- 0.6
maf.filter <- 0.01

poverty_sumstats <- sumstats(files = files, ref = ref, trait.names = trait.names, se.logit = se.logit, OLS = OLS, linprob = NULL,
                             N = NULL, betas = NULL, info.filter = info.filter, maf.filter = maf.filter, parallel = TRUE, cores = 3)

# Write the formatted sumstats to a file for debugging purposes
write.table(poverty_sumstats, "poverty_sumstats_formated.txt", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

# Run common factor GWAS
poverty_factor <- commonfactorGWAS(covstruc = hi_sd_oi_LDSCoutput, SNPs = poverty_sumstats,
                                   estimation = "DWLS")

write.table(poverty_factor, "poverty_factor.txt", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

# Print all warnings
warnings()
